title: Vacaville City Councilmember Sarah Chapman wins the city's mayoral race following fellow councilmember Roy Stockton congratulating her, which came shortly after the Solano County Registrar of Voters' latest update reporting Chapman in the lead by 155 votes, with all outstanding votes counted. As of the registrar's latest update at 4:45 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Chapman has 17,516 votes, holding 50.22 percent of the vote over her opponent. With the number of county-wide curable ballots at 432 — Vacaville's share in that pile unknown — Chapman's position may not have changed much by the time the registrar officially calls the race, tentatively, Dec. 5. Stockton posted an announcement on Facebook an hour after the registrar's update, extending his gratitude to supporters, and congratulating Chapman alongside Tom Chalk and John Vogel in their successes in the Districts 2 and 4 races, respectively. "I want to congratulate Sarah Chapman on her election as Vacaville's next Mayor," he wrote in the post. "I wish her success as we move forward in serving our community." Chapman added six votes to her total since last Friday, Nov. 13, when the registrar began their hand-count audit — a process of checking for missed ballots or errors. "We've gone through a whole bunch of polling places, a whole bunch of vote by mail ballots," Assistant Registrar of Voters John Gardner said on the hand-counting audit process. "So we just keep trucking through it, and we really haven't seen anything come up yet." The process consists of drawing random batches of ballots from different Solano County polling places, along with a chip that instructs which contests get re-counted by hand for that group — which, for example, could be an individual race, a page of the ballot, or every contest in the ballot. "Various levels of contests are counted. Various levels of ballots are in each batch." Gardner added. The registrar's update includes only small changes to the county's other city council races, further solidifying the counts. Districts 2, 4 and 6. Tom Chalk is still leading with 4,078 votes, or 56.54 percent of the vote, against Gregory Ritchie's campaign for re-election in District 2. In the District 4 race — Chapman's seat — John Vogel maintains his lead with 2,150 votes, or 52.67 percent of the vote, against Davonna Finley. Jeanette Wylie is on track to win another term in her District 6 seat against Kevin Puett, with 4,132 votes, or 64.25 percent of the vote. Chapman has a Ph.D in Public Policy and Administration and a Master's in Public Administration/Manpower Management. She has been a board member for the Vacaville Unified School and Library Districts, and a trustee for Solano Community College. She is endorsed by Solano Orderly Growth, the Napa-Solano Building and Construction Trades Council and the Northern Solano Democratic Club, among others. District 1's Stockton is also a sergeant at the Solano County Sheriff's Department, and has two decades of law enforcement experience. He is endorsed by Vacaville's Police Officers Association, the local chapter of the International Association of Firefighters, Vacaville Chamber of Commerce and the Northern Solano County Association of Realtors, among others. The audit will continue through next Wednesday, Nov. 25, and a report will be posted at certification. Next Wednesday at 5 p.m. is also the last day for voters to resolve signature issues on their ballots.

title: Military airstrikes kill 21 ISWAP fighters, commanders in Borno Air strikes by the Nigerian military have left 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters dead in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State. The operations, carried out by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI, between November 16 and 17, also targeted the group's explosives network and killed some of its senior commanders. The Army in a statement on Wednesday said the first strike followed intelligence reports that ISWAP fighters were advancing towards Monguno. It said an unmanned aerial vehicle deployed to monitor the area spotted the fighters moving along a bush path northeast of the town. The Army added thatva subsequent strike killed seven fighters, including members of the group's Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network. Among them was ABBA BOMMA, identified as a key explosives expert. Four others sustained severe injuries. It said at Arinna, in the South Lake Chad area, a second operation targeted the group's leadership and fighters. Those killed included MALLAM SHARKI, a member of ISWAP's Shura Council and Amirul Amini (Provost Commander), and ABU SAAD, identified as the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu. Twelve other fighters died in the strike, while five sustained severe injuries. Several motorcycles belonging to the group were also destroyed. The Army said the two operations left 21 fighters dead and 10 others severely injured, with the strikes disrupting ISWAP's IED network and weakening its command structure.
